name: SignalSave
title: Signal Save
description: Save the people the organisation engages to Signal, without reading anyone back.
whenToUse: Pick to record a person the organisation is engaging, prospects and customers, when the caller may add people but must not read Signal: an Agent that finds leads, a workflow that saves what a search found. Signal finds a person again by their LinkedIn, email or app account, so saving twice updates rather than duplicates. The answer is only whether it was saved, never the record. To find or list people, Signal People.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The person to save, in save_person's shape: at least one of linkedin, email or user_id, and whatever else was found. The organisation is the run's own.

outputs.name: saved
outputs.description: Whether it was saved and nothing more: ok, created, person_id, or the reason it was not

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: signal
package.packageFile:
# SIGNAL — who a person is and what happens next (docs/architecture/signal/README.md). Signal
# holds everyone the organisation engages, prospects and customers, one record per person per org
# (SIGNAL.md § 4a, ruled 2026-10-09). The record is the memory service's; these nodes reach it
# through the engine at loopback, as the dataset package does, so no node knows its address.
name: signal
displayName: Signal
description: Save and read the people the organisation engages, prospects and customers
version: 0.1.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Save one person, found again by their LinkedIn, their email or their app account, never made twice
  - Find one person, and list the organisation's prospects and customers, as an Agent's tools
  - Keep what research found about them in Signal's layers (observed, understood, inferred)
  - Open and keep an Agent's own goals for a person, never another's, without reading anyone

allowedHosts:
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before saving or finding a person. The
# wording IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing is a
# behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.

people:
  name: Signal People
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Save and find the people the organisation engages, in Signal, its own record of them.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL PEOPLE PROTOCOL:
    - save_person needs at least one way to recognise the person: linkedin, email or user_id.
      It finds the person already held by those, strongest first, and updates them, or makes them.
    - Only what you pass is written; anything left out keeps its old value. Each layer you pass
      (observed, understood, inferred, researched) replaces that layer whole.
    - Never pass a value you were not given or did not find. Leave it out rather than guess.
    - Whether a person is a prospect or a customer is Signal's to decide, never yours.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was saved.
  methods:
    save_person:
      description: >-
        Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update
        them, or make them. Returns the person as now held, with their id, and whether they are new.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          linkedin:
            type: string
            description: Their LinkedIn profile URL or handle.
          email:
            type: string
            description: Their email address.
          user_id:
            type: string
            description: Their app account id, when they have signed in.
          name:
            type: string
            description: Their full name.
          company:
            type: string
            description: The company they work for now.
          role:
            type: string
            description: Their role there.
          crm_provider:
            type: string
            description: The CRM that also holds them, such as hubspot.
          crm_id:
            type: string
            description: Their record's id in that CRM.
          category:
            type: string
            enum: [customer, partner, procurement, not-now]
            description: >-
              What they are to us: customer (would buy for their own business), partner (would
              build and deliver it for their clients), procurement (approves suppliers) or not-now
              (not someone we write to yet). Only a customer is written to.
          observed:
            type: object
            description: >-
              Facts found about them: location, the company's domain and website, their email and
              what it rests on (emailBasis), their pictures each with the page it came from, their
              employers with dates, and the news that names them.
            properties:
              location: { type: string, description: Where they are based. }
              domain: { type: string, description: Their company's web domain. }
              website: { type: string, description: Their company's website address. }
              emailBasis: { type: string, description: What their email address rests on. }
              pictures:
                type: array
                description: Pictures of them, their profile photo first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    url: { type: string, description: The picture's own address. }
                    page: { type: string, description: The page it came from. }
              employers:
                type: array
                description: Their employers, latest first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    company: { type: string }
                    role: { type: string }
                    from: { type: string, description: When they started, as found. }
                    to: { type: string, description: When they left; empty while they are there. }
              inTheNews:
                type: array
                description: News that names them, latest first.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    title: { type: string, description: The story's headline. }
                    what: { type: string, description: What the story says of them, in a line. }
                    source: { type: string, description: The publication. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
          understood:
            type: object
            description: >-
              What has been learned: what they care about (each point with its exact quote, date
              and link), how they decide, where they have spoken (title, kind, date, link), what is
              live at their company.
            properties:
              whatTheyCareAbout:
                type: array
                description: What they care about, each point with their exact words.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    point: { type: string, description: The point, in a few words. }
                    quote: { type: string, description: Their exact words. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string, description: Where they said it. }
              howTheyDecide:
                type: array
                description: How they decide, one line each.
                items: { type: string }
              spokenAt:
                type: array
                description: Where they have spoken.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    title: { type: string }
                    kind: { type: string, description: A talk, a podcast, a panel, an interview. }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
              companyNow:
                type: array
                description: What is live at their company now.
                items:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    headline: { type: string }
                    date: { type: string }
                    url: { type: string }
          inferred:
            type: object
            description: >-
              What follows from it: why they would want what the organisation offers (whyUs: the
              reason, the quote it rests on, the part of the offer that answers it), the questions
              to ask, what to avoid.
            properties:
              whyUs:
                type: object
                description: Why they would want what the organisation offers.
                properties:
                  reason: { type: string, description: The reason, in a sentence. }
                  quote: { type: string, description: Their exact words it rests on. }
                  quoteUrl: { type: string, description: Where they said it. }
                  partOfOffer: { type: string, description: The part of what the organisation offers that answers it. }
              questions:
                type: array
                description: The questions to ask them.
                items: { type: string }
              whatToAvoid:
                type: array
                description: What to avoid with them.
                items: { type: string }
          researched:
            type: object
            description: The sources used and how sure the identity is.
            properties:
              sources:
                type: array
                description: The address of every source used.
                items: { type: string }
              confidence: { type: string, description: How sure the identity is, and why. }
    find_person:
      description: >-
        Find one person Signal holds, by their id, LinkedIn, email or app account. Returns
        found false when Signal holds nobody by that.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          id:
            type: string
            description: Their Signal person id.
          linkedin:
            type: string
            description: Their LinkedIn profile URL or handle.
          email:
            type: string
            description: Their email address.
          user_id:
            type: string
            description: Their app account id.
    list_people:
      description: >-
        The people Signal holds for this organisation, most recently updated first, optionally
        only one stage or one segment.
      input:
        type: object
        properties:
          stage:
            type: string
            enum: [prospect, customer]
            description: Only people at this stage.
          category:
            type: string
            enum: [customer, partner, procurement, not-now]
            description: Only people in this segment.
          limit:
            type: number
            description: How many, at most 200. Default 50.

# SIGNAL SAVE (docs/architecture/signal/AGENTS.md § 7a): the same save, for a caller that may add
# people but not read them. Its input IS save_person's above, never a copy; its answer is only
# whether it was saved, never the person as held.
save:
  name: Signal Save
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Save the people the organisation engages to Signal, without reading anyone back.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL SAVE PROTOCOL:
    - save_person needs at least one way to recognise the person: linkedin, email or user_id.
      It finds the person already held by those, strongest first, and adds to them, or makes them.
    - It only ever adds: an empty field is filled, a list gains what it lacks, and nothing held is
      overwritten or removed. Pass what you found; what is held stays.
    - Never pass a value you were not given or did not find. Leave it out rather than guess.
    - The answer says only whether it was saved, the person's id and whether they are new. It never
      shows what Signal already held about them.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was saved.
  methods:
    save_person:
      description: >-
        Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update
        them, or make them. Returns only whether it was saved, their id and whether they are new.
      input: { $ref: schema#/people/methods/save_person/input }

# SIGNAL GOALS (docs/architecture/signal/AGENTS.md § 7c): a person's goals, for a caller that may
# add people but not read them: it opens, reads, saves and finishes them. Every call names its
# caller, from the run, never the model: the goal records who opened it, and an Agent's every
# change is on the audit trail. Goals live here only (Signal People keeps people); no answer
# carries a person's record.
goals:
  name: Signal Goals
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: Open and keep the goals for the people Signal holds, without reading anyone.
  instructions: |-
    SIGNAL GOALS PROTOCOL:
    - A goal is what we want with one person next. open_task needs the person's Signal id, the
      goal's task URI and what it holds to start with; save_person answers the id.
    - save_task replaces what the goal held: write everything it now holds, history included.
    - A goal rests on what you found about them: research first, and give each fact with its link
      in rests_on. A goal with nothing under it is refused, and so is one for a person whose
      Signal record does not yet say what you found about them: save that to them first.
    - Each step names one of your own tasks, the one you will run for it. A step naming any other is
      refused.
    - finish_task closes a goal for good, with whether it was met and why.
    - A tool that answers ok: false carries the reason. Say so rather than claiming it was done.
  methods:
    find_tasks:
      description: >-
        Every goal Signal holds for one person, newest first: open ones with what they hold and
        when their next step is due, finished ones with what they finished with.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task:
            type: string
            description: Only this goal's task, by its URI (unoverse://tasks/<org>/<name>).
    open_task:
      description: >-
        Open a goal for one person Signal holds: the goal's task URI, what it holds to start with,
        and when its next step is due. Answers the goal's id.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task, state]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task:
            type: string
            description: The goal's task URI, unoverse://tasks/<org>/<name>.
          state:
            type: object
            description: What the goal holds, in these parts.
            properties:
              outcome:
                type: string
                description: The conversation we want with them, in one line.
              why_now:
                type: string
                description: The real, current reason to reach them, from what you found.
              why_now_link:
                type: string
                description: The link that reason comes from.
              rests_on:
                type: array
                description: What the goal rests on, from your research. At least one, each a fact you found with its link.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [fact, link]
                  properties:
                    fact: { type: string, description: One thing you found, as found. }
                    link: { type: string, description: Where you found it. }
              ideas:
                type: array
                description: What we would bring them, each a short sentence.
                items: { type: string }
              learn:
                type: array
                description: What we want to learn from them for this goal, each with why it helps them. Asked in the conversation, never as a form.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [what]
                  properties:
                    what: { type: string, description: The thing to learn, such as the children's heights. }
                    why: { type: string, description: Why it helps them, said the way we would say it to them. }
              steps:
                type: array
                description: The steps to get there, each one of your own tasks on a day of the goal, never a date, so the goal runs whenever it starts.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [day, task, what]
                  properties:
                    day: { type: integer, description: "Its day in the goal: 0 for the first step, then 5, 12. Each step is due that many days after the step before it was done, its day less theirs." }
                    task: { type: string, description: The URI of one of your own tasks, the one you will run for this step. }
                    what: { type: string, description: What the step brings them. }
                    phase: { type: string, description: "Where the step falls in the journey, in a few words, such as Before arrival, In the hotel, night 2, or After the stay. Optional." }
                    result: { type: string, description: What came of it; empty until it happens. }
                    run: { type: string, description: "The id of the task run that did this step, as the task's reply gives it (its run), so the step opens what it made. Empty until it happens." }
                    app: { type: string, description: "The app its run opens in, by name, when it should open in one (any app opens any task, MCP_TASKS.md § 5c). Empty opens the task alone." }
                    done: { type: string, description: The date it was done (ISO 8601); empty until it happens. }
            required: [outcome, rests_on, steps]
          wake_at:
            type: string
            description: When its next step is due (ISO 8601), from the date the step before it was done. Empty until the first step is done.
    save_task:
      description: >-
        Save an open goal for one person: everything it now holds, and when its next step is due.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task_id, state]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task_id:
            type: string
            description: The goal's id, as open_task or find_tasks gave it.
          state:
            type: object
            description: Everything the goal now holds, in these parts. Replaces what it held.
            properties:
              outcome:
                type: string
                description: The conversation we want with them, in one line.
              why_now:
                type: string
                description: The real, current reason to reach them, from what you found.
              why_now_link:
                type: string
                description: The link that reason comes from.
              rests_on:
                type: array
                description: What the goal rests on, from your research. At least one, each a fact you found with its link.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [fact, link]
                  properties:
                    fact: { type: string, description: One thing you found, as found. }
                    link: { type: string, description: Where you found it. }
              ideas:
                type: array
                description: What we would bring them, each a short sentence.
                items: { type: string }
              learn:
                type: array
                description: What we want to learn from them for this goal, each with why it helps them. Asked in the conversation, never as a form.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [what]
                  properties:
                    what: { type: string, description: The thing to learn, such as the children's heights. }
                    why: { type: string, description: Why it helps them, said the way we would say it to them. }
              steps:
                type: array
                description: The steps to get there, each one of your own tasks on a day of the goal, never a date, so the goal runs whenever it starts.
                items:
                  type: object
                  required: [day, task, what]
                  properties:
                    day: { type: integer, description: "Its day in the goal: 0 for the first step, then 5, 12. Each step is due that many days after the step before it was done, its day less theirs." }
                    task: { type: string, description: The URI of one of your own tasks, the one you will run for this step. }
                    what: { type: string, description: What the step brings them. }
                    phase: { type: string, description: "Where the step falls in the journey, in a few words, such as Before arrival, In the hotel, night 2, or After the stay. Optional." }
                    result: { type: string, description: What came of it; empty until it happens. }
                    run: { type: string, description: "The id of the task run that did this step, as the task's reply gives it (its run), so the step opens what it made. Empty until it happens." }
                    app: { type: string, description: "The app its run opens in, by name, when it should open in one (any app opens any task, MCP_TASKS.md § 5c). Empty opens the task alone." }
                    done: { type: string, description: The date it was done (ISO 8601); empty until it happens. }
            required: [outcome, rests_on, steps]
          wake_at:
            type: string
            description: When its next step is due (ISO 8601), from the date the step before it was done. Empty until the first step is done, and when nothing is due.
    finish_task:
      description: >-
        Finish an open goal for one person, with what it finished with: met or not, and why. Kept,
        never reopened.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [person_id, task_id, result]
        properties:
          person_id:
            type: string
            description: The person's Signal id (person_id).
          task_id:
            type: string
            description: The goal's id.
          result:
            type: object
            description: What it finished with, such as { met, reason } and the final values.

# WHAT A GOAL MUST HOLD, checked before it is opened or saved (goals, above): it rests on facts
# found, each with its link, and each step names one of the calling Agent's own tasks. On opening,
# Signal must already know them: their record's `understood` holds something (their company now,
# where they spoke). A goal written from nothing, for someone we do not know, or naming a task the
# Agent does not have, is refused with the reason.
helpers:
  goalProblem:
    args: [state, agents, caller, person]
    body: >-
      return (() => {
        const s = state || {};
        const known = Object.values((person && person.understood) || {}).some(v => Array.isArray(v) ? v.length > 0 : !!v);
        if (person && !known) return 'NOT_KNOWN: Signal knows nothing about ' + (person.name || 'them') + ' yet. Research them and save what you found to their record first.';
        const facts = Array.isArray(s.rests_on) ? s.rests_on.filter(f => f && f.fact && f.link) : [];
        if (!facts.length) return 'NO_RESEARCH: a goal rests on what you found about them. Research first, then give rests_on: each fact with its link.';
        const me = (agents || []).find(a => 'agent:' + a.ref === caller);
        if (!me) return '';
        const mine = me.tasks || [];
        const bad = (Array.isArray(s.steps) ? s.steps : []).map(x => (x && x.task) || '(none)').filter(t => !mine.includes(t));
        return bad.length ? 'NOT_YOUR_TASK: ' + bad.join(', ') + '. Each step names one of your own tasks: ' + mine.join(', ') : '';
      })()

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order. Only whether it was saved: the record the
# save returns never leaves this node.
- emit: saved
  value: >-
    return response && response.ok && response.person_id
      ? { ok: true, created: !!response.created, person_id: response.person_id }
      : { ok: false, error: (response && response.error) || 'NOTHING_TO_SAVE: the input names no linkedin, email or user_id' }
files.api/run.yaml:
# The WORKFLOW channel: save the person on the input, as the attached Agent's save_person does
# (service.yaml), so a workflow can record what a search found with no Agent in between. Skipped
# when the input names no way to recognise the person; the events row says so.
- name: save
  when: >-
    return !!((signal.input || {}).linkedin || (signal.input || {}).email || (signal.input || {}).user_id)
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/people/add'"
  okOn: [400, 409]
  body: "return Object.assign({}, signal.input || {}, { org: scope.org })"
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 30000
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return String(response.error)"
files.api/service.yaml:
# ADD ONLY (AGENTS.md § 7a): the engine at loopback, then the memory service's `people` table, by
# `/people/add`, which never overwrites or removes what is held: an empty field is filled, a list
# gains what it lacks. A caller that cannot read a person can add to them and never wipe them. The
# answer is only whether it was saved, never the record.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for Signal Save
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#save }

save_person:
  description: >-
    Save one person to Signal: find them by their LinkedIn, email or app account and update them,
    or make them. Returns only whether it was saved, their id and whether they are new.
  calls:
    - name: save
      method: POST
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/people/add'"
      okOn: [400, 409]
      # `by`, the run's caller from its scope, after the model's params so it cannot be set by them:
      # the engine keeps it off the record and puts an Agent's change on the audit trail (§ 7c).
      body: "return Object.assign({}, params, { org: scope.org, by: scope.userId })"
      transport: json
      timeoutMs: 30000
  returns: >-
    return calls.save && calls.save.ok && calls.save.person_id
      ? { ok: true, created: !!calls.save.created, person_id: calls.save.person_id }
      : { ok: false, error: (calls.save || {}).error || 'NOT_SAVED' }
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: >-
      The person to save, in save_person's shape: at least one of linkedin, email or user_id, and
      whatever else was found. The organisation is the run's own.
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: saved
    type: object
    description: "Whether it was saved and nothing more: ok, created, person_id, or the reason it was not"

credentials: []

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [save_person]
    description: >-
      MCP tool for an agent: save_person (find by LinkedIn, email or app account, then update or
      make). Answers only whether it was saved, never the record.
    instructions: >-
      save_person needs at least one of linkedin, email or user_id. Only what you pass is written;
      each layer passed replaces that layer whole. Never pass a value you were not given or did
      not find. Whether a person is a prospect or a customer is Signal's to decide.
files.node.yaml:
type: SignalSave
kind: PromiseNode
name: Signal Save
category: Storage & Data
color: "#334155"
template: service
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png
description: Save the people the organisation engages to Signal, without reading anyone back.
whenToUse: >
  Pick to record a person the organisation is engaging, prospects and customers, when the caller
  may add people but must not read Signal: an Agent that finds leads, a workflow that saves what a
  search found. Signal finds a person again by their LinkedIn, email or app account, so saving
  twice updates rather than duplicates. The answer is only whether it was saved, never the record.
  To find or list people, Signal People.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13; docs/architecture/signal/AGENTS.md § 7a). Adding
# a person is `signal:write`, apart from reading everyone (`signal:read-all`, Signal People), so a
# caller that finds leads never needs to read every contact and user to save one.
auth:
  required: true
  role: signal:write

capabilities:
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# A save with no way to recognise the person is refused by Signal before anything is written, so
# the fixture writes nothing: the answer is ok false, with the reason, and never a record.
testData:
  config: {}
  call:
    method: save_person
    params:
      name: Nobody In Particular
  expect:
    output: "return output.ok === false && typeof output.error === 'string' && output.person === undefined"
